open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock read scope
open_points.text: “one reading per request” conflicts in scope with “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps” and the audit writer exception that “the writer takes it when it appends”
open_points.question: Does “request” mean one HTTP request, one use-case operation, or one call to system_clock.utc_now, and does audit_writer take an additional reading during the same HTTP request?
options: One wall reading for the entire HTTP request, shared by authorization, use case and audit writer
One wall reading per use-case operation, with audit_writer taking its own additional reading
One host-clock read per call to system_clock.utc_now, with no request-wide limit
open_points.default_guess: Treat each use-case operation as taking one wall reading and let audit_writer take the explicitly permitted additional reading.

witness.initial: An active staff account submits a login request that will create a session and append staff.login.
events: staff_identity.authenticate_staff needs the current instant for the session timestamps and expiry
audit_writer.append_audit needs occurred_at for the audit record
outcomes: Under a request-wide reading, both modules share one wall-clock value and the host wall clock is read once
Under the per-operation rule and audit exception, staff_identity and audit_writer call utc_now separately and may persist different instants
witness.observer: A verification harness instrumenting system_clock, and an operator inspecting the persisted session and audit timestamps

open_points.subject: wall-clock use in State 4 flows
open_points.text: “An operation that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses it” is added, but the State 4 steps that create, revoke, expire, update or audit records name no capability:system_clock.utc_now call or caller.
open_points.question: For each affected flow step, which owning operation calls system_clock.utc_now, at what point, and which nested writes and validity comparisons receive that instant?
options: Each owning use-case capability calls utc_now itself once and passes the value to its internal work
The route delegate calls utc_now once and supplies it to authorization and the owning use case
A transaction or request coordinator calls utc_now and shares it among all operations in the flow
open_points.default_guess: Have each owning use-case capability call utc_now once immediately before its first time-dependent comparison or record construction, with audit_writer using its documented separate reading.

witness.initial: A viewer has a live credential, live sessions, and an administrator re-issues the credential.
events: viewer_access.issue_viewer_access revokes the old credential and sessions, creates the new credential and appends an audit
outcomes: viewer_access explicitly calls system_clock.utc_now once and reuses that instant for all viewer-owned writes
The route or a transaction coordinator obtains the instant and supplies it to viewer_access
witness.observer: The State 6 contract author and the flow-reachability verification, which must choose a caller and dependency path for utc_now

open_points.subject: viewer-entry elapsed-clock step
open_points.text: “the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry window from it,” while flow:viewer_entry_and_session only says the guard “has already rate-limited entry” and names no capability:system_clock.monotonic_seconds call.
open_points.question: Which transport-guard step calls monotonic_seconds, and is it called only for viewer-entry requests or once for every HTTP request before route classification?
options: transport_guard calls monotonic_seconds once only after identifying a viewer-entry request
transport_guard calls monotonic_seconds once for every HTTP request and uses it only for viewer-entry rate limiting
runtime obtains the elapsed reading and passes it to transport_guard
open_points.default_guess: Have transport_guard call monotonic_seconds once only for a request identified as viewer entry, before credential verification.

witness.initial: The service receives one ordinary health request followed by one viewer-entry request.
events: transport_guard processes and rate-limits the viewer-entry request
outcomes: Only the viewer-entry request reads the elapsed clock
Both requests read the elapsed clock, although only the second reading affects a rate-limit bucket
witness.observer: A transport-guard verification harness instrumenting system_clock

open_points.subject: system_clock failure outcome
open_points.text: The new system_clock capabilities specify returned values but name no failure type or outcome when the host wall or elapsed clock cannot be read.
open_points.question: What must each flow do if system_clock.utc_now or system_clock.monotonic_seconds fails before or during an operation?
options: Fail the request closed with a declared internal-service failure and leave every transaction unchanged
Treat clock failure as an unhandled runtime failure
Refuse service startup or readiness after clock failure
open_points.default_guess: Fail closed as a declared internal-service failure; roll back any open transaction and write nothing, with no retry or fallback clock.

witness.initial: A viewer-entry request reaches transport_guard while the elapsed-clock backend fails.
events: transport_guard attempts to obtain the rate-limit timestamp before verifying the access secret
outcomes: The request fails closed with a defined 500-class response and never reaches viewer_access
The clock exception is unhandled, or the guard proceeds without rate limiting
witness.observer: The viewer and the runtime operator, who see a controlled response versus an unhandled failure or a request admitted without the required rate limit
